Where it began

Axar Patel was born in Nadiad, in Gujarat, on 20 January 1994. He came through as a bowling all-rounder for Gujarat, bowling slow left-arm spin and batting left-handed, and he took his first six-wicket haul against Delhi late in 2013, in just his second first-class game.

That Ranji Trophy season he made 369 runs and took 29 wickets, and he helped India's under-23 side win the Emerging Teams Cup in 2013. The board named him its under-19 cricketer of the year for 2012/13.

The player

His first one-day international came against Bangladesh in June 2014, and he was in India's squad for the 2015 World Cup. Test cricket kept him waiting until February 2021, when England came to India. He made the wait worthwhile. His first Test wicket was Joe Root, he took five in an innings on debut, and in three Tests that series he took 27 wickets at 10.59.

He played 15 Tests between 2021 and 2025. In them he took 57 wickets at 19.67, with five five-wicket innings, one ten-wicket match and a best of 6 for 38. He also made 688 runs at 34.40, with four fifties and a top score of 84.

What made him special

Axar's great gift was taking wickets cheaply. A Test bowling average under 20 is the sort of figure most spinners only dream about. With the bat he was a hard hitter who liked to finish the job: his first one-day fifty, 64 not out from 35 balls against the West Indies in 2022, ended with a six to win the match.

By November 2026 the one thing missing from his Test record was a hundred. He got as far as 84, a few blows short. Spinners are meant to be patient people.

Away from the middle

In the shorter formats he became a regular for India. He was part of the sides that won the T20 World Cup in 2024 and again in 2026, and the Champions Trophy in 2025. In the 2024 semi-final against England he was player of the match, and in the final he struck 47 from 31 balls with four sixes. In July 2025 he became the first Indian spinner to take 100 wickets in T20 internationals.

In the IPL he played for Punjab and later captained Delhi Capitals, and back in 2016 he took a hat-trick, four wickets in five balls against Gujarat Lions.

And finally

His first IPL contract was with Mumbai Indians in 2013. He did not play a single game that season, and Mumbai won the title anyway. It may be the only trophy he ever collected without bowling a ball.
